claim: mRNA profiles were measured in 15 yeast species from the phylum Ascomycota
source_text: Here, we used a phylogenetic framework to measure mRNA profiles in 15 yeast species from the phylum Ascomycota
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the experimental data collection described in the manuscript, including the species-specific microarrays and RNA profiling experiments.

claim: The study reconstructs the evolution of modular regulatory programs over 300 million years
source_text: reconstruct the evolution of their modular regulatory programs along a time course of growth on glucose over 300 million years
evidence_reasoning: The 300 million year timespan is based on phylogenetic analysis and the experimental data collected across the 15 species allows reconstruction of evolutionary trajectories.

claim: Modules have diverged proportionally to phylogenetic distance
source_text: We found that modules have diverged proportionally to phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by correlation analyses between expression profiles and phylogenetic distances shown in Figure 3 and related statistical tests.

claim: Prominent changes in gene regulation accompany changes in lifestyle and ploidy, especially in carbon metabolism
source_text: with prominent changes in gene regulation accompanying changes in lifestyle and ploidy, especially in carbon metabolism
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum analysis showing coordinated reassignment of carbon metabolism genes at phylogenetic points associated with lifestyle changes.

claim: Paralogs have significantly contributed to regulatory divergence, typically within a very short window from their duplication
source_text: Paralogs have significantly contributed to regulatory divergence, typically within a very short window from their duplication
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum analysis showing that approximately 53% of paralogs that eventually change module assignment do so at their point of duplication.

claim: Paralogs from a whole genome duplication (WGD) event have a uniquely substantial contribution that extends over a longer span
source_text: Paralogs from a whole genome duplication (WGD) event have a uniquely substantial contribution that extends over a longer span
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis showing WGD paralogs continue to be enriched among reassigned genes at multiple phylogenetic points after the WGD event.

claim: Similar patterns occur in the evolution of the heat shock regulatory program measured in eight of the species
source_text: Similar patterns occur when considering the evolution of the heat shock regulatory program measured in eight of the species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data from heat shock experiments and references to Roy et al., 2013 which describes these experiments in detail.

claim: Divergence in gene regulation can play a major role in evolution
source_text: Divergence in gene regulation can play a major role in evolution
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established principle in evolutionary biology supported by multiple citations and general scientific knowledge.

claim: Examples of regulatory differences between species were described in bacteria, fungi, flies, and mammals
source_text: Examples of regulatory differences between species were described in a wide range of species including bacteria (McAdams et al., 2004), fungi (Gasch et al., 2004; Habib et al., 2012), flies (Prud'homme et al., 2007; Wittkopp et al., 2008; Bradley et al., 2010), and mammals (Khaitovich et al., 2006; Odom et al., 2007; Brawand et al., 2011; Lindblad-Toh et al., 2011; Perry et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the cited references to previous studies in these organisms.

claim: The mechanisms through which regulatory systems evolve are still only partially understood
source_text: However, the mechanisms through which regulatory systems evolve are still only partially understood
evidence_reasoning: This represents a consensus view in the field supported by the cited references discussing gaps in understanding.

claim: The adaptive importance of regulatory changes is unknown in most cases
source_text: and in most cases the adaptive importance of regulatory changes is unknown
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Lynch, 2007 and other references discussing the challenge of determining adaptive significance.

claim: Gene duplication can promote regulatory divergence by either neo-functionalization or sub-functionalization
source_text: it has been suggested (Lynch and Force, 2000; Gu et al., 2004, 2005; Teichmann and Babu, 2004; ; Conant and Wolfe, 2006; Tirosh and Barkai, 2007; Wapinski et al., 2007b) that gene duplication can promote regulatory divergence by either neo-functionalization or sub-functionalization of regulatory mechanisms of the two paralogs
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical framework supported by multiple cited studies and represents established models in evolutionary biology.

claim: The 15 Ascomycota species span >300 million years of evolution
source_text: Here, we use comparative transcriptional studies across 15 Ascomycota species—spanning >300 million years of evolution (Sipiczki, 2000)
evidence_reasoning: The timespan is based on phylogenetic estimates from the cited reference (Sipiczki, 2000).

claim: The study collected approximately 300 expression profiles at six physiologically comparable time points
source_text: We optimized culture conditions across species, and collected ∼300 expression profiles at six physiologically comparable time points along each species' growth
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental data collection performed in the study.

claim: The six time points sampled are repletion (lag phase), exponential growth ('mid-log' and 'late log'), the point of glucose depletion ('diauxic shift') and two later time points when the growth rate levels off ('post shift' and 'plateau')
source_text: repletion (lag phase), exponential growth ('mid-log' and 'late log'), the point of glucose depletion ('diauxic shift') and two later time points when the growth rate levels off ('post shift' and 'plateau')
evidence_reasoning: This describes the specific experimental design and sampling strategy used in the study.

claim: Arboretum is a new algorithm used to identify expression modules across species and reconstruct their evolutionary history
source_text: To analyze the evolution of regulatory modules, we use a new algorithm, Arboretum (Roy et al., 2013), to identify expression modules across species and to reconstruct their evolutionary history
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational method developed and applied in this study, with reference to its detailed description.

claim: The transcriptional response involves five major transcriptional modules in all species
source_text: In all species, the transcriptional response involves five major transcriptional modules
evidence_reasoning: This is the result of applying the Arboretum algorithm to the expression data collected across all species.

claim: Module expression patterns are conserved across species
source_text: While the module's expression patterns are conserved across species, their gene membership diverges
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum analysis showing similar temporal expression patterns for modules across species despite changes in gene membership.

claim: Module gene membership diverges proportionally to phylogenetic distance
source_text: While the module's expression patterns are conserved across species, their gene membership diverges, proportionally to phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the AMCI analysis showing correlation between phylogenetic distance and module conservation.

claim: Species in the Kluyveromyces, Candida, and Yarrowia clades are respiratory and use oxidative phosphorylation
source_text: Species in the Kluyveromyces, Candida, and Yarrowia clades are respiratory and use oxidative phosphorylation
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge about these species' metabolic characteristics and is consistent with the growth data collected.

claim: A respiro-fermentative lifestyle has evolved independently at least twice in this phylogeny, once after the WGD and once in Schizosaccharomyces
source_text: Conversely, a respiro-fermentative lifestyle—a preference to ferment glucose even in the presence of oxygen (Piskur et al., 2006)—has evolved independently at least twice in this phylogeny, once after the WGD (Conant and Wolfe, 2007) and once in Schizosaccharomyces (Rhind et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on phylogenetic analysis and cited references about the metabolic characteristics of these lineages.

claim: K. polysporus has an intermediate phenotype between respiro-fermentative and respiratory
source_text: K. polysporus, the most basal post-WGD species (Scannell et al., 2007) has an intermediate phenotype between respiro-fermentative and respiratory
evidence_reasoning: This is based on growth data collected in the study and the phylogenetic position of this species from cited references.

claim: Y. lipolytica is an obligate respiratory species that can uniquely use normal hydrocarbons and various fats as carbon sources
source_text: Y. lipolytica (Figure 1A, green) is an obligate respiratory species, but can uniquely use normal hydrocarbons and various fats as carbon sources (Kurtzman, 2000)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge about Y. lipolytica from the cited reference.

claim: The optimized growth medium boosts the growth of otherwise slow growers without substantially impacting the growth of fast growers
source_text: Our formulation boosts the growth of otherwise slow growers, without substantially impacting the growth of fast growers
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the growth curve data comparing species performance in the optimized medium vs standard media.

claim: The degree of divergence of the transcriptional profiles correlates with phylogenetic distance
source_text: We find that the degree of divergence of the transcriptional profiles correlates with phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by correlation analyses between expression profile similarity and phylogenetic distance shown in Figure 3.

claim: The largest divergence occurs in lag phase profiles
source_text: with the largest divergence in lag phase profiles
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the correlation analysis showing lag phase has the lowest correlation between species compared to other time points.

claim: Gene duplication events significantly contribute to regulatory divergence, in particular close to their phylogenetic point of duplication
source_text: Gene duplication events significantly contribute to regulatory divergence, in particular close to their phylogenetic point of duplication
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the enrichment analysis showing paralogs are significantly enriched among reassigned genes at their point of duplication.

claim: The contribution of WGD paralogs to regulatory divergence is more pronounced and more prolonged than other paralogs
source_text: This contribution is more pronounced and more prolonged for WGD paralogs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis showing WGD paralogs remain enriched among reassigned genes at multiple phylogenetic points after the WGD.

claim: The correlation in expression decreases with phylogenetic distance
source_text: We found that the degree of correlation is inversely related with the phylogenetic distance between the species (r<−0.39 to −0.77, p<3 × 10−5, Figure 3B–F)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis of the correlation between expression profiles and phylogenetic distances.

claim: Profiles at diauxic shift, post shift and plateau are the most correlated between species
source_text: Profiles at diauxic shift, post shift and plateau are the most correlated between species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3D-G.

claim: Lag profiles are the most divergent between species
source_text: whereas the lag profiles, when cells 'reset' in response to nutrient repletion, are the most divergent
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the correlation analysis showing lag phase has the lowest average correlation between species.

claim: S. japonicus and S. castellii were the most divergent species
source_text: S. japonicus and S. castellii were the most divergent
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the expression profile correlation analysis across species.

claim: In some cases, lag phase profiles of S. japonicus and S. castellii were anti-correlated to those of other species
source_text: such that in some cases, their Lag phase profiles were even anti-correlated to those of other species, suggesting distinct repletion programs
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis of expression profiles showing negative correlations for these species.

claim: Growth genes such as mRNA splicing genes are enriched among the highly induced genes in lag phase across most species
source_text: Nevertheless, some functional groups of genes do exhibit conserved induction or repression in the lag phase across most species (e.g., growth genes such as mRNA splicing genes are enriched among the highly induced genes [p<10−5, FDR, 'Materials and methods']
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes induced in lag phase.

claim: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model of the evolution of module membership
source_text: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model of the evolution of module membership of a given gene, starting from the last common ancestor (LCA) of a set of species and probabilistically propagating this membership down the branches of the phylogenetic tree to the leaf nodes
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational method developed and is supported by the reference to Roy et al., 2013.

claim: Arboretum uses the phylogeny to link the module IDs at each phylogenetic point to the modules of the LCA
source_text: Arboretum uses the phylogeny to link the module IDs at each phylogenetic point to the modules of the LCA
evidence_reasoning: This describes a key feature of the Arboretum algorithm as implemented in the study.

claim: Arboretum uses the structures of gene trees during module identification
source_text: and uses the structures of gene trees (as defined from genome sequences; Wapinski et al., 2007a) during module identification
evidence_reasoning: This describes how the algorithm incorporates gene phylogenies from previous work.

claim: Arboretum allows genes to change their module assignment during evolution
source_text: Arboretum allows genes to change their module assignment during evolution
evidence_reasoning: This describes a key feature of the algorithm's design.

claim: At any ancestral or extant species, every gene must be assigned to exactly one module for a particular response
source_text: but at any ancestral or extant species, every gene (if present in that species) must be assigned to exactly one module for a particular response
evidence_reasoning: This describes a constraint in the Arboretum model.

claim: Module 1 consists of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis
source_text: Module 1: Ribosome biogenesis, p<5.28 × 10−48 to 1.25 − 10−119, fraction 37.3–61.6%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes in Module 1.

claim: Module 2 consists of genes involved in cell division
source_text: Module 2: cell division, p-value<3.51 × 10−02 to 4.52 × 10−02, fraction 9–33.6%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes in Module 2.

claim: Module 3 consists of genes involved in cell morphogenesis
source_text: Module 3: cell morphogenesis, p<4.64 × 10−02 to 4.95 × 10−02, fraction 6.5–81%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes in Module 3.

claim: Module 4 consists of genes involved in mitochondrial function and proteasome
source_text: Module 4: mitochondrial, p<3.20 × 10−02 to 4.90 × 10−02, fraction 2.4–37.9%; proteasome, p<3.85 × 10−04 to 3.97 × 10−02, fraction 1.6–15%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes in Module 4.

claim: Module 5 consists of genes involved in respiration and response to stress
source_text: Module 5: respiration p<4.77 × 10−02 to 4.8 × 10−02, fraction 32.6–58.9%; response to stress, p<4.75 × 10−02 to 4.86 × 10−02, fraction 2.6–13.7%
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of genes in Module 5.

claim: Modules conserve their gene members relative to their immediate ancestor inversely to phylogenetic distance
source_text: Modules conserve their gene members relative to those of their immediately ancestral internal vertex in the tree ('immediate ancestor'), inversely to phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the AMCI analysis showing correlation between conservation and phylogenetic distance.

claim: The AMCI is calculated as the mean of the diagonal entries of the transition matrix
source_text: The AMCI is calculated as the mean of the diagonal entries
evidence_reasoning: This describes the mathematical definition of the AMCI metric used in the analysis.

claim: AMCI decreases with increased phylogenetic distance
source_text: The correlation between branch length and AMCI is −0.68 (p≤1.13 −× 10−4)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis showing significant negative correlation between AMCI and branch length.

claim: Module 1 and Module 5 are the most phylogenetically conserved
source_text: Genes assigned in the LCA to Modules 1 (Figure 4B, blue entries) and 5 (Figure 4F, red entries) tend to persist in those modules (Module Stability 94% ± 0.5% and 84% ± 1.2%, respectively, 'Materials and methods')
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the module stability analysis showing high persistence of genes in these modules.

claim: Modules 2, 3, and 4 are less stable with more frequent reassignment of their member genes to other modules
source_text: Conversely, Modules 2, 3, and 4 (Figure 4C–E) are less stable, with more frequent reassignment of their member genes to other modules
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the module stability analysis showing lower persistence in these modules.

claim: Module 1 and 5 are the least dynamic as reflected by the average proportion of genes that join or leave each module
source_text: Module 1 and 5 are the least dynamic as reflected by the average proportion of genes that join (11% ± 1.6% and 17% ± 1.7%, respectively) or leave each module (6% ± 0.4% and 16% ± 1%, respectively)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Module Expansion Index and Module Contraction Index calculations.

claim: Cell cycle and DNA replication genes are reassigned in a coordinated fashion from Module 3 in the LCA to Modules 4 and 5 in post-WGD species
source_text: For example, cell cycle and DNA replication genes are reassigned in a coordinated fashion from Module 3 in the LCA to Modules 4 and 5 in
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum module assignment analysis showing coordinated transitions of functionally related genes.

claim: Mitochondrial genes are reassigned en masse in both post-WGD and Schizosaccharomyces species
source_text: Particularly substantial transitions in module assignment are associated with changes in carbon lifestyle during the transitions to respiro-fermentation post-WGD and in
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis of module reassignments showing coordinated changes in mitochondrial gene regulation.

claim: Respiratory genes have lost the binding site for the transcription factor Sfp1 in many respirofermentative species
source_text: In addition, the promoters of mRP and respiration genes have lost the binding site for the transcription factor Sfp1 (previously identified as the 'Rapid Growth Element', RGE; Ihmels et al., 2005) in many respirofermentative species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by motif enrichment analysis in promoter regions and cited previous work.

claim: The Sfp1 binding site is strongly conserved in 'growth' (Module 1) genes across all species except S. japonicus
source_text: The Sfp1 binding site is strongly conserved in 'growth' (Module 1) genes across all species (except S. japonicus) and serves as an ancient regulatory tether of the growth module (p<0.05, Hyper-geometric test; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by motif enrichment analysis showing significant enrichment of Sfp1 sites in Module 1 genes.

claim: Purine metabolism and amino acid catabolism genes in pathways that feed nucleotide synthesis are reassigned from Module 1 to Module 5 in post-WGD species
source_text: Indeed, more surprisingly, purine metabolism and amino acid catabolism genes in pathways that feed nucleotide synthesis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum module assignment analysis and metabolic pathway analysis.

claim: Genes that have a paralog were more likely to change their module assignment than those present in a single copy
source_text: Genes that have a paralog were more likely to change their module assignment than those present in a single copy (KS test, p<1.5 × 10−107)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison of reassignment rates between duplicated and non-duplicated genes.

claim: Paralogous genes are much more likely to be reassigned after duplication than their corresponding pre-duplication orthologs
source_text: Furthermore, controlling for any differences in function between duplicated and non-duplicated genes, paralogous genes are much more likely to be reassigned after duplication than their corresponding pre-duplication orthologs (Figure 10D,E, KS test, p<1 × 10−18)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison of reassignment rates before and after duplication events.

claim: Increased divergence was most prominent at the WGD ancestor (A5) and the Schizosaccharomyces ancestor (A13)
source_text: This increased divergence was most prominent at the WGD ancestor (A5) and the Schizosaccharomyces ancestor (A13)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the AMCI analysis showing the largest decreases in conservation at these phylogenetic points.

claim: Both the WGD and Schizosaccharomyces ancestors have a larger number of retained paralog pairs compared to other ancestral species
source_text: Both ancestors also have a larger number of retained paralog pairs compared to other ancestral species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of gene trees and duplication events at different phylogenetic points.

claim: The WGD and Schizosaccharomyces ancestors reside at the points of the independent evolution of respiro-fermentation
source_text: and reside at the points of the (independent) evolution of respiro-fermentation
evidence_reasoning: This is based on phylogenetic analysis and known metabolic characteristics of these lineages.

claim: The reassigned paralogs are enriched in carbon metabolism genes
source_text: Consistently, the reassigned paralogs are enriched in carbon metabolism genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis of reassigned paralogous genes.

claim: Approximately 60% of the paralog pairs that arose at the ancestor of the Candida clade (A10) and that will eventually change their assignment do so at that ancestor
source_text: For example, ∼60% of the paralog pairs that arose at the ancestor of the Candida clade (A10) and that will eventually change their assignment, do so at that ancestor
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module reassignment timing for paralogs that arose at specific phylogenetic points.

claim: Of all the paralog pairs that arose sporadically in the phylogeny, 53% are reassigned at the point at which they arose
source_text: Overall, of all the paralog pairs that arose sporadically (not in the WGD) in the phylogeny, and where at least one member of the pair was subsequently reassigned to a different module, 53% do so 'at' the point at which they arose
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of the timing of module reassignment relative to duplication events.

claim: Sporadically duplicated genes are significantly enriched among all the reassigned genes at their point of duplication, but not at later phylogenetic points
source_text: Furthermore, such sporadically duplicated genes are significantly enriched (Hyper-geometric test, p<0.05,) among all the reassigned genes (duplicated or not) at their point of duplication, but not at later phylogenetic points
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by enrichment analysis comparing the proportion of paralogs among reassigned genes at different phylogenetic points.

claim: There is a short 'window of opportunity' in regulatory innovation specifically facilitated by paralogous genes shortly after they are duplicated but not later
source_text: This suggests a short 'window of opportunity' in regulatory innovation, specifically facilitated by paralogous genes shortly after they are duplicated but not later
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the enrichment pattern of paralogs among reassigned genes being specific to the point of duplication.

claim: WGD paralogs continue to be enriched among reassigned genes at multiple phylogenetic points after the WGD event
source_text: Paralogs that arose in the WGD
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by enrichment analysis showing WGD paralogs remain enriched among reassigned genes at later phylogenetic points.

claim: Segmental duplication rarely preserves the entire regulatory region resulting in immediate expression divergence
source_text: This may be explained by the fact that segmental duplication rarely preserves the entire regulatory region resulting in immediate expression divergence (Lynch and Katju, 2004)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on cited knowledge about the mechanisms of segmental duplication.

claim: Duplicates from WGD events preserve the regulatory inputs and thus may take longer to diverge
source_text: whereas duplicates from WGD events preserve the regulatory inputs and thus may take longer to diverge
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the known characteristics of WGD events and the observed prolonged divergence pattern.

claim: Mitochondrial and respiratory genes were reassigned en masse in both independent evolutions of respiro-fermentation
source_text: In both cases, mitochondrial and respiratory genes were reassigned en masse, accompanied by convergent cis regulatory changes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the Arboretum analysis showing coordinated reassignment of these genes in both lineages.

claim: Changes in the regulation of amino acid, purine and sulfur metabolism genes occurred only following the WGD
source_text: However, changes in the regulation of amino acid, purine and sulfur metabolism genes occurred only following the WGD
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the module reassignment analysis showing these changes are specific to the post-WGD lineage.

claim: Changes in amino acid, purine and sulfur metabolism gene regulation may have occurred by repositioning of cis-regulatory elements relative to nucleosome free regions
source_text: possibly by repositioning of cis-regulatory elements relative to nucleosome free regions
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanism supported by nucleosome positioning analysis showing changes in motif positioning relative to NFRs.

claim: Many of the changes in carbon metabolism occurred gradually, with only some noticeable in K. polysporus
source_text: The post-WGD event can be monitored in fine phylogenetic resolution, showing that many of the changes occurred gradually, with only some noticeable in K. polysporus, the first species to have diverged post-WGD
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments in K. polysporus showing intermediate patterns between pre- and post-WGD species.

claim: Respiro-fermentation is functionally analogous to the Warburg Effect in cancer cells
source_text: Respiro-fermentation is functionally analogous to the (somatically evolved) Warburg Effect in cancer cells (Vander Heiden et al., 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge about metabolic similarities between these phenomena, supported by the cited reference.

claim: There are well-known similarities in glycolysis and respiration between respiro-fermentation and the Warburg Effect
source_text: There are well-known similarities in glycolysis and respiration between the two states that enable both cancer and yeast cells to direct glucose to biosynthesis, supporting their rapid growth and proliferation
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge in the field about metabolic similarities.

claim: The causes of the Warburg Effect metabolic signature and its connection to biosynthesis are not fully understood
source_text: However, both the causes of this metabolic signature and its connection to biosynthesis are not fully understood
evidence_reasoning: This represents a known gap in understanding in cancer metabolism research.

claim: Genes encoding enzymes in the nucleotide salvage and glycine biosynthesis pathways are strongly induced post-diauxic shift in respiro-fermentative post-WGD species
source_text: The observation that genes encoding enzymes in the nucleotide salvage and glycine biosynthesis pathways are strongly induced post-diauxic shift in respiro-fermentative post-WGD species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the expression data and module assignment analysis.

claim: Changes in nucleotide salvage and glycine biosynthesis pathways in cancer cells that display the Warburg Effect are analogous to changes in respiro-fermentative yeasts
source_text: is analogous to recently identified changes in these pathways in cancer cells that display the Warburg Effect (Gaglio et al., 2011; Jain et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on comparison with cited studies of cancer cell metabolism.

claim: Rewiring of nucleotide biosynthetic pathways contributes to the respiro-fermentative phenotype
source_text: suggests that rewiring of nucleotide biosynthetic pathways contributes to this phenotype
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the observed coordinated changes in nucleotide metabolism genes in respiro-fermentative species.

claim: Most paralogs (66% of all pairs) have at least one member diverging from the ancestral module
source_text: Most paralogs (66% of all pairs) have at least one member diverging from the ancestral module
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments of paralog pairs relative to their pre-duplication ancestor.

claim: 27% of paralog pairs show classical neo-functionalization where one paralog maintains the ancestral assignment and the other is assigned to a different module
source_text: This includes paralogs with distinct fates, either due to 'classical' neo-functionalization (27% of all pairs), where one paralog maintains the ancestral assignment and the other is assigned to a different module
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog pair fates from the Arboretum analysis.

claim: 12% of paralog pairs show asymmetric divergence where each paralog is reassigned to a distinct module, each different than the ancestral one
source_text: or due to asymmetric divergence (12%), where each paralog is reassigned to a distinct module, each different than the ancestral one
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog pair fates from the Arboretum analysis.

claim: 27% of paralog pairs show symmetric divergence where both paralogs are reassigned to the same module, distinct from the ancestral one
source_text: In the remaining cases (27%) there is symmetric divergence, where both paralogs are reassigned to the same module, distinct from the ancestral one
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog pair fates from the Arboretum analysis.

claim: Only 34% of paralog pairs conserve the ancestral assignment of both copies
source_text: Only in a minority of paralog pairs (34%) the ancestral assignment of both copies is conserved
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog pair fates from the Arboretum analysis.

claim: The pre-duplication orthologs of neo-functionalized genes are most prominent in the 'unchanged' Module 3 and mildly induced Module 4
source_text: The pre-duplication orthologs of genes from the neo-functionalized class are most prominent in the 'unchanged' Module 3 and mildly induced Module 4 (Hyper-geometric test, p<10−3)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by enrichment analysis of the ancestral module assignments of neo-functionalized paralogs.

claim: Genes that were not regulated in glucose depletion prior to duplication 'gain' such regulation de novo post-duplication for at least one paralog
source_text: suggesting that genes that were not regulated in glucose depletion prior to duplication, 'gain' such regulation de novo post-duplication, for at least one paralog
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the enrichment of neo-functionalized genes in modules with little or no regulation pre-duplication.

claim: Neo-functionalization has contributed to the regulatory divergence of key genes in carbon metabolism during the evolution of respiro-fermentation
source_text: Neo-functionalization has also contributed to the regulatory divergence of key genes in carbon metabolism during the evolution of respiro-fermentation (Figure 8B), consistent with previous studies (Conant and Wolfe, 2007)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of carbon metabolism gene paralogs and cited previous work.

claim: The evolutionary trajectories of paralogous genes are highly similar between heat shock and glucose depletion
source_text: Furthermore, the evolutionary trajectories of paralogous genes—including the higher reassignment of paralogs, the distinct reassignment capacity of sporadic and large-scale duplications, and the preponderance of reassignment of only one of two paralogs—are highly similar between heat shock and glucose depletion
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by comparative analysis of paralog behavior in both conditions.

claim: The patterns observed are general evolutionary principles, at least in this phylogeny
source_text: This suggests that these are general evolutionary principles, at least in this phylogeny
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the observation of similar patterns in two independent conditions.

claim: The median Pearson correlation between biological replicates is 0.97
source_text: The collected replicates were very highly reproducible (median Pearson correlation between replicates is 0.97, Figure 3—source data 1)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis of the correlation between biological replicates.

claim: The microarray profiles are highly correlated to corresponding profiles measured using RNA-Seq data
source_text: Furthermore, the microarray profiles are highly correlated to corresponding profiles measured using RNA-Seq data generated from RNA extracted from the same plateau and mid-log time point samples. This is true both when considering all genes (0.835 < r < 0.958, mean r = 0.913, 0.0362 SD)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparison of microarray and RNA-Seq measurements from the same samples.

claim: Custom microarray designs accurately distinguish paralogs and estimate their expression levels
source_text: indicating that our custom microarray designs accurately distinguish paralogs and estimate their expression levels
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the high correlation between microarray and RNA-Seq data for paralogous genes.
